content.title: About
content.content: The “American and Swiss” cheese blend combines processed American cheese with Swiss cheese featuring characteristic holes. It has a smooth, slightly creamy texture, a moderately sharp flavor, and a pleasant aroma, suitable for both hot and cold dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: American cheese was created in the early 20th century in the USA as a cost‑effective cheese alternative.
Swiss cheese (Emmental) is known for its “eyes,” formed by carbon dioxide released by bacteria.
The blend merges the meltability of American cheese with the aromatic notes of Swiss, making it popular in fast‑food applications.
It is commonly used in sandwiches, burgers, casseroles, and fondue.
Combining the two cheeses improves stretchability and gives a richer taste than either cheese alone.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Cheese is rich in calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Protein
items.content: Provides high‑quality dairy protein that supports tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamins B2 and B12, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Phosphorus
items.content: Phosphorus contributes to cellular function and nervous system health.

items.title: Probiotic cultures
items.content: Swiss cheese includes live bacteria that can benefit gut health.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The blend contains lactose, so individuals with intolerance should limit intake.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: It can be salty; excess sodium may increase blood pressure risk.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some people may experience allergic reactions to casein.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Cheese is high in fat and calories, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use the blend in hot sandwiches, burgers, casseroles, pasta dishes, or as a cold topping for salads and appetizers. It can be sliced thinly or melted into sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cheese in the refrigerator at 2‑4 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container. For longer storage, it can be frozen, though texture may change.
